summary: The hidden units produce the XOR truth table correctly. The toy demonstrates a fixed nonlinear circuit; it does not learn XOR from examples.

claims.claim: A single linear decision boundary cannot represent XOR; hidden nonlinear units can.
claims.how: The fixed hidden units compute OR and NAND; their final threshold computes XOR for all four input pairs.

sources.title: Multilayer perceptrons
sources.says: Hidden layers with nonlinear activations extend the functions a linear classifier can represent.

claims.claim: The XOR output is one when exactly one input is one.
claims.how: The actual XOR helper returns 0, 1, 1, 0 for 00, 01, 10, 11.

sources.title: Half adder
sources.says: A half adder produces XOR for the sum and AND for the carry. Two half adders and an OR gate form a full adder.

claims.claim: The picture illustrates a multilayer network, not a trained model.
claims.how: The weights and thresholds are stored constants; tapping cycles the four input cases.

sources.title: Multilayer perceptrons
sources.says: Hidden layers with nonlinear activations extend the functions a linear classifier can represent.

simplified: The XOR network uses fixed threshold units. Its truth table is real, but there is no loss calculation or training step.
